record.paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
record.original_question: Can non-real-representability of a matroid given by a rank oracle be certified using only a polynomial number of rank evaluations?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.5. Can non-R-representability be certified using only a polynomial number of rank-evaluations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let M be a matroid on a finite ground set E of size n, given by a rank oracle: a black box that, on input S ⊆ E, returns the rank r_M(S) ∈ ℤ_{≥0} in a single call. The matroid M is said to be ℝ-representable if there exist a vector space V over ℝ and a map φ: E → V such that for every S ⊆ E, the rank r_M(S) equals the dimension of the linear span of φ(S); otherwise M is non-ℝ-representable.

A certificate of non-ℝ-representability of M, relative to the rank oracle, is a finite list (S_1, r_1), …, (S_k, r_k) of pairs with S_i ⊆ E and r_i = r_M(S_i), such that every matroid M' on E whose rank function agrees with M on the sets S_1, …, S_k is also non-ℝ-representable. The size of the certificate is k.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial p(n) such that every non-ℝ-representable matroid on n elements admits a certificate of non-ℝ-representability of size at most p(n)? Equivalently, can non-ℝ-representability always be witnessed using only polynomially many rank evaluations?
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous question for prime fields GF(p) was answered positively (O(n^2) rank evaluations suffice). However, for the reals no such polynomial certificate is known, and the problem of certifying non-ℝ-representability with polynomially many rank evaluations is posed as an open problem. Recent work showing that real matroid representability is ∃ℝ-complete suggests substantial obstacles, but does not resolve the rank-oracle certification question. No source verifies a resolution.

status_evidence.title: Certifying Non-representability of Matroids Over Prime Fields
status_evidence.snippet: Showing that an n-element matroid is not representable over GF(p) requires only O(n^2) rank evaluations.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the prime-field analogue but does not address the real case.

status_evidence.title: Representing Matroids over the Reals is ∃ℝ-complete
status_evidence.claim: Indicates inherent hardness of real representability but does not resolve the polynomial-certificate question in the rank-oracle model.
